design:
D1 Hazard and rollback (Tier 2). Migration 0124 creates vault_settings on :8000's real database at its next restart, and the bundle reaches :8000's app at its next reload, in either order (the tab's 404 state covers the gap). Rollback is the downgrade, which drops the table and loses only the two settings. Vault files are never touched by a migration. A tracked upload writes into the operator's working tree, and nothing else in the repository is changed. Also new: the Hub writes files outside any project, at the private location. It writes only there, and only under paths built from Hub-minted ids.

D2 The map in every turn is a capped index (operator, 2026-10-09, F573 a). There is one line per entry (id, type, name, and the holder when the text is elsewhere), cut at 2,000 characters, and the section is absent when the vault is empty. It sits in the per-turn part of the context (agents.py, the part_starts split), because it changes with every upload, and Copilot's stable part is written once into its agent file.

D3 A private location inside the project is refused (operator, 2026-10-09, F573 b). The default, ~/.agentweave/hub/vaults/<project id>, is the Hub's own data directory, so the operator never has to choose. Refusal is checked on resolved paths, so neither a symlink nor a .. component can get past it. The worktrees are inside the project, so they are covered too.

D4 File layout. knowledge/sources/<id>.md holds the raw text, and <id>.json beside it holds id, name, type, visibility, created_at, holder and media type. A private entry has the same pair at the private location, and a stub under knowledge/sources holds the metadata without the text. Sources are never rewritten: an upload always mints a new id.

D5 No index table yet. The map is built from the record files on each read. That is enough at the size a vault reaches by hand, and it means a colleague's pulled files appear with no import step. A table arrives when a later slice needs to query entries, such as fetch counts in access-tuning.

D6 A stub reveals its name, type and holder (roadmap D3). That is the cost of colleagues knowing the entry exists. The upload form says so when private is chosen.

D7 The holder is this machine's network name (platform.node()). There is no other identity for a person on a local Hub.

D8 Text arrives as a JSON string, not a multipart upload. This keeps the route free of a new dependency, and the app reads a chosen file as text in the browser. Images and PDFs bring their own route in their slice.

lifecycle: When closed, this change folds into a new knowledge-vault capability, and the roadmap's vault-text-sources slice is then done.
problem: The knowledge vault roadmap (spdoc-7c75066d6403) needs a place to put business knowledge before anything can be distilled from it. Today a transcript reaches an agent only by being pasted into one conversation. Nothing keeps it for the next conversation, another harness, or a colleague on the same project. The manager framework now exists (hub/hub/manager.py), but its jobs would have nothing to read. This slice is the vault's floor: the operator can put sources in, people can read them, and agents can find them and read them, without any model in the loop.

requirements.rationale: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-09 (F573 b): a private location inside the repository is refused. A private folder inside the working tree can be swept into a commit by git add -A, or become tracked when .gitignore changes. Worktrees live at .agentweave/worktrees inside the project (project_workspace.py:58).
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/settings MUST answer private_location, effective_private_location and default_visibility. With nothing stored, private_location is null, effective_private_location is ~/.agentweave/hub/vaults/<project id>, and default_visibility is tracked. PUT MUST store either field. It MUST answer 400 and change nothing when private_location is relative, is inside the project's directory (its worktrees included), or cannot be created; it MUST also answer 400 when default_visibility is neither tracked nor private.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D2: files are the record, one file per source so merges stay clean. D3: tracked by default, and a private entry is a stub in the map. The id is minted by the Hub (src- followed by 12 hex characters), so no caller-chosen name ever becomes a path.
requirements.statement: POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/sources with name, type and content MUST answer 201 with the entry as the map lists it. visibility is optional and falls back to the project default. A tracked source MUST be written as knowledge/sources/<id>.md (the text, byte for byte) plus knowledge/sources/<id>.json (its metadata) under the project's directory. A private source MUST be written the same way at the effective private location, and only a stub (id, name, type, visibility, holder, created_at) MUST be written as knowledge/sources/<id>.json; no part of the text may be written inside the project. The route MUST answer 400 for an empty name, a name over 200 characters, a type outside transcript, document, rules, example and note, or empty content. It MUST answer 413 for content over 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D2 and D5: a source is in the map the moment it is uploaded, with no model involved. A colleague who pulls knowledge/ has none of this Hub's rows, so the map is read from files.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/map MUST answer {"entries": [...]}, newest first. It is built on every read from knowledge/sources and the effective private location. Each entry holds id, name, type, visibility, created_at, holder, available, and opening. opening is the source's first non-blank lines, joined and cut at 300 characters, and is null when the text is not on this machine. A private source held on this machine MUST be listed once, from its full record. A stub whose text is not here MUST be listed with available false.

requirements.rationale: A transcript can be longer than one tool result. Paging by offset keeps every answer bounded without a file round-trip.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/entries/{entry_id}?offset=N MUST answer the entry as listed, plus content: at most 50,000 characters of the text from offset N (default 0), and next_offset, which is null when the text ends within that page. For an entry whose text is not on this machine, it MUST answer 200 with available false, content null, and a sentence naming the holder. An unknown or malformed id MUST answer 404.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D6: only the manager writes. Agents read the map freely and fetch by id.
requirements.statement: Working agents MUST have two read-only tools, vault_map() and vault_read(entry_id, offset=0), answering what map-listed and entry-read answer, through the agent-actions routes under the run's own credentials. They MUST be on every runner's tool surface (MCP, the call-mode command, and Copilot's allowlist). No agent-callable route may write to the vault.

requirements.rationale: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-09 (F573 a): a capped index. With nothing in the turn, agents would not know the vault exists. The whole map would cost more with every upload, on every turn and for every agent.
requirements.statement: When the project's map holds at least one entry, every turn's context MUST include a Knowledge vault section in its per-turn part. The section names vault_read, then gives one line per entry, newest first: id, type, name, and for an entry not available here, the holder. The lines are cut so that the section stays within 2,000 characters, and a last line then says how many entries were left out and that vault_map lists them all. When the map is empty, the section MUST be absent.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D9: a cloud backend is a later implementation of this interface, not a rewrite.
requirements.statement: Every vault read and write MUST go through one storage interface (write a record, read a record, list records under a root), whose only implementation in this slice is the local filesystem. The routes MUST work unchanged when a test substitutes another implementation.

requirements.rationale: It runs on :8000's real database at its next restart. It creates a table only; nothing existing is copied or changed.
requirements.statement: The migration MUST create vault_settings (project_id primary key, private_location nullable, default_visibility not null, default tracked, updated_at). Its downgrade MUST drop the table and touch no vault file.

requirements.rationale: A committed bundle reaches :8000's app on its next reload, possibly before its server restarts (the same hazard as the manager section).
requirements.statement: The app's project view MUST have a Vault tab. It lists the map's entries, opens an entry's text, uploads a source (name, type, visibility starting at the project default, the text pasted or read from a chosen text file), and shows and changes the two settings, showing the Hub's 400 message when the Hub refuses a setting. Where the Hub answers 404 for the vault routes, the tab MUST say that this Hub has no vault yet, instead of failing.

in_scope: Vault settings per project: the private location and the default visibility (tracked or private), with a migration for their table
Upload of a text source with a name, a type, the text, and optionally a visibility
One storage interface with a local filesystem backend, used for every vault read and write
A map built from the record files on every read: tracked entries, private entries held on this machine, and stubs of private entries held elsewhere
Reading one entry by id, in pages
Two read-only agent tools, vault_map and vault_read
A capped index of the map in every turn's context
A Vault tab in the app: the list, an entry's text, upload, and the two settings
non_goals: Facts, contradictions, reports and any manager job: these are later slices
Images, PDFs and binary files: text only in this slice
Editing or deleting a source: sources are raw and never edited, and deleting one is left for later
Committing the files: the Hub writes knowledge/ into the working tree, and the operator's own git flow commits it
A database index of entries, and fetch counting (access-tuning slice)
Any agent-callable write to the vault

summary: A project gets a knowledge vault. The operator uploads text sources such as meeting transcripts, business rules and example documents, and reads them in a Vault tab. A source is tracked under knowledge/ in the repository by default, so colleagues share it. The operator can also make it private: it is then stored at a location outside the repository, and only a stub names it under knowledge/. Every source enters the map the moment it is uploaded, with its name, type and opening lines; no model is involved. Working agents see a short index of the map in every turn, and read entries through two read-only tools. Tier 2: a new table and migration, the first upload route, and files written outside the repository.
